dataset: WBDS -- Fukuchi, Fukuchi & Duarte (2018), a public data set of overground and treadmill walking
record_used: five subjects (WBDS01-05), treadmill walking. For each, two time-aligned blocks: KINEMATICS = sagittal knee + ankle flexion angles, KINETICS = the antero-posterior + vertical ground reaction force, down-sampled to 450 time-aligned samples. These are the SAME blocks used by the distance-correlation and RSA/Mantel cases.
pipeline: markers -> sagittal knee + ankle flexion angles alongside the AP+vertical GRF -> PhysioCrossModal::cca(X, Y), Hotelling's canonical correlation analysis: the linear combinations of the two blocks that are maximally correlated, returning the canonical correlations. The reference recomputes the SAME canonical correlations with base R's stats::cancor. Deterministic.
note: Canonical correlation analysis (Hotelling 1936) finds the maximal LINEAR correlation between two multivariate blocks. The tracked inputs are eval/data/crossmodal-dcor/ (kinematics_wbds01.rds + kinetics_wbds01.rds for the terminal proof; blocks_5subj.rds for robustness) -- reused from the dCor / RSA cases so the three cross-modal lenses run on identical data. cca reproduces base R's stats::cancor (a non-trivial, independent SVD computation) to machine precision (max |diff| = 1.1e-16). The first canonical correlation (0.737) is close to the distance correlation on the same data (0.72), indicating the kinematics-kinetics coupling is largely linear -- captured by the first canonical pair.
